formula_checks.name: theTaxOrganizer
formula_checks.why: Rounds account income before handing it to another tax calculator and uses mixed trailing paid/estimated account income for an explicit tax year. Reinvested taxable income may be omitted.
formula_checks.should_be: Retain full precision, select the stated tax year, separate actual records from estimates and include taxable reinvested distributions for taxable accounts. Supply the delegated tax organizer’s public formula.

formula_checks.name: taxableAnnual
formula_checks.why: Treats all retirement cash receipts as taxable income, including full Social Security and withdrawals, without taxable-fraction/account-basis data.
formula_checks.should_be: Separate cash receipts from taxable amounts by source/account; compute Social-Security taxable fraction and qualified Roth/tax-basis treatment, or mark estimate/incomplete.

formula_checks.name: taxedAfterPreTax
formula_checks.why: Correct identity only with correctly scoped taxable income and contributions; the text says paid-month contributions while the legacy household annual helper uses12.
formula_checks.should_be: Use sum(householdK401ByMonth) and corrected source-specific taxable amounts; preserve unknowns.

formula_checks.name: filingStatusOf
formula_checks.why: The formula reads filing status, but the purpose wrongly describes a tax-rate function. Missing status is inferred from spouse presence rather than a confirmed filing election.
formula_checks.should_be: Correct the purpose; label inferred status and ask/allow correction, never present it as confirmed.

formula_checks.name: stateRateOf
formula_checks.why: Converts an explicitly entered percent to a fraction within the documented0–15% estimate range; absence must be labeled as no state estimate, not known0 tax.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: monthlyTaxRates
formula_checks.why: Uses the same household rate in every month as explicitly decided; this is a budgeting allocation, not IRS actual paycheck withholding.

formula_checks.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
formula_checks.why: Floors each month’s taxable amount at0, discarding negative net rental/business income; summing months can exceed taxableAnnual.
formula_checks.should_be: Preserve signed eligible losses and apply any annual statutory limits at the annual tax calculation, not monthly clipping.

formula_checks.name: over65CountOf
formula_checks.why: Defaults a joint household with an unanswered spouse-age question to the person’s age alone; January1 birthdays and unknown eligibility require the IRS age rule.
formula_checks.should_be: Preserve unknown spouse age/eligibility and use the statutory end-of-tax-year age test including January1 convention; label estimates.

formula_checks.name: effectiveRate
formula_checks.why: Delegates to the same authoritative rate without a second calculation.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: effectiveTaxRate
formula_checks.why: Calculated branch ignores entered state tax and uses a separate gross/status path instead of the one rateInForce promised throughout the app.
formula_checks.should_be: Delegate to rateInForce with the same taxable-income/401(k)/state inputs, or retire this incompatible reader.

Year-month preservation is present in canonical wage tables,but annualized/converted paths and yearless vest/one-time defaults lose the same dated meaning.
rules_held.decision_in_force:
When you enter a year of income, the app asks which twelve months you mean — the calendar year, or the next twelve months from now. Three decisions:
1. Every month you enter carries its own month AND year, so entering across a New Year does not overwrite the wrong month.
2. Both ways of asking write to the same twelve calendar slots underneath, so the answer means the same thing however it was entered.
3. When a receipt is scanned, the total is read from the total — never from a line about how it was paid, which is not what you spent.

rules_held.decision_in_force:
The whole income surface redesigned. Six decisions:
1. Base pay becomes a full screen with one expandable section per earner — gross, 401(k), employer match, and what actually lands.
2. A 14-month dated table when pay varies, rather than one typical figure.
3. BOTH earners are captured, not one: a household on $84,000 plus $54,000 was being read as $84,000 — one person’s income against two people’s spending.
4. A filing-status question, which had never been asked, so every couple was taxed as a single filer.
5. Bonus and company shares follow the same who-earns pattern.
6. Interest and dividends are worked out from your holdings rather than asked for, and treated as TAXABLE BUT NOT SPENDABLE.

What it is taxed on was left as drawn, each gross line, then Gross a year.
